newsitem.title: USA: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - April 16.
newsitem.headline: U.S. midweek cash lumber review - April 16.

text.p: Random Lengths Gross List Cash Lumber Prices Quotes:

Comment - Sellers maintained the upper hand in lumber trading through Tuesday, Random Lengths said in its midweek update. Some species traded at a moderate pace but others saw a fair amount of carryover from last week's run. Wholesalers and distributors gained a good deal of business with quick shipment.
Pipeline inventories were not heavy and many dealers' stocks remained thin, the lumber reporting agency said. Persistent rail car shortages frustrated buyers and sellers.

Western S-P-F trading focused on the secondary level. Office wholesalers and distributirs sold quick wood readily at a few dollars below mill quotes. Buyers resisted the May 5 shipping times quoted by many mills, but producers raised prices $2-8 and picked off some sales. The tightest width was #2&Btr 2x10. Rail shipments remained congested in some areas, Random Lengths said.
Eastern S-P-F mills raised prices as steady demand fed stronger order files. All #1&2 2-inch items rose $5-10, it said.
Many eastern dealers looked to secondaries for quick fill-ins rather than wait for mill shipments. In studs, dry 2x4 pre-cuts jumped $10-15, the reporting agency said.

Southern Pine sales maintained a brisk pace. Some producers were slow to raise prices, preferring to let order files grow. But others pushed quotes aggressively and wide spreads developed. The 2x6 was strongest, followed closely by 2x10.
Canadian exports remained muted, with fee-free shipments as of April 8 at 1.6 percent of annual April/March quota.
Inland dimension prices rose but with Hem-Fir at a hefty premium to Coast and North California, buyer resistance rose.
Wides of Fir-Larch sold at $600 or higher. ES-LP and Fir&Larch precut studs also sold readily; Hem-Fir lagged. Ponderosa Pine 1x12 prices eroded, it said.

Coast Hem-Fir and dry Douglas fir trading was active and prices rose. The #2&Btr 2x10 was the most-sought width in both species; some mills sold Hem-Fir for shipment the week of May 5. Fir prices gained $6-15 and jumps in Hem-Fir spanned the $10-15 range. Stud prices advanced; Douglas fir precuts rose $15.

Southern Pine plywood sales were slow and prices held. Some mills sold slightly above reported prices; others with thin order files conceded $2-3. Scattered weather problems slowed demand and caused some log shortages, Random Lengths said.

Western plywood prices flattened in response to an uneventful start to the week's trading. Mills moved light volumes of sheathing and underlayment while secondaries focused on selling from inventories. Secondaries had difficulty selling at replacement costs and made at least modest concessions.

OSB prices showed spot gains in mixed trading. Dealers bought hand-to-mouth while mills refrained from building order files at current levels. Secondaries undercut mill quotes in most markets. L-P-s Corrigan, Texas, plant was expected to be down for 10-12 days for maintenance.
